title: British Voters Choose to Exit EU, PM Cameron to Step Down
main_content:
In a historic decision, Britain has voted to leave the European Union in a referendum that stoked passions on issues of immigration and sovereignty.

The “Leave” cause won 51.89 percent of the vote. The news prompted a negative reaction in Asian markets and the British pound tumbled to a three-decade low.

The vote appeared to be driven by anti-establishment sentiments and the feeling that the EU governing structure has taken too much control away from the common British citizen.

“Let June 23 go down in our history as our independence day,” anti-EU campaigner Nigel Farage, told supporters in Westminster early Friday. Farage heads Britain’s UK Independence Party, which favors implementing tough immigration restrictions.

Analysts say that disengagement may take two or more years to complete.

Voters appeared to have defied calls by government and business, which forecast dire economic consequences for Britain. The British treasury predicted that leaving the EU would cost the average family nearly $6,000 a year.

Business leaders warned that new immigration restrictions that could result from a Brexit would cause them to transfer thousands of British jobs to countries still in the EU.

In the end, British voters appeared to choose the risk of independence over what many Leave supporters view as overreach by an undemocratic EU governing apparatus that is only getting bigger and more intrusive.

questions.question: What were some immediate economic consequences of the result of the vote?
options: The British pound tumbled to a three-decade low and Asian markets reacted negatively.
The British treasury announced an increase in taxes to stabilize the economy.
Stock prices soared in anticipation of new trade deals.
Consumer confidence increased as a result of the independence sentiment.
questions.answer: The British pound tumbled to a three-decade low and Asian markets reacted negatively.

questions.question: What were the “Leave” voters motivated by?
options: A desire for increased EU regulations and a strengthening of economic ties.
Frustration with government and business predictions of economic downturn.
Anti-establishment sentiments and the belief that the EU exerted too much control.
A wish for more extensive multicultural integration across European nations.
questions.answer: Anti-establishment sentiments and the belief that the EU exerted too much control.

questions.question: What will the financial cost of the exit be?
options: The British treasury predicts it will save families nearly $6,000 a year.
The average family is estimated to lose approximately $6,000 annually.
There will be no immediate financial repercussions as the exit is negotiated.
Financial impacts are not quantifiable as they depend on future trade negotiations.
questions.answer: The average family is estimated to lose approximately $6,000 annually.
